---
title: "When does camdl run a model again?"
description: "Where camdl keeps the results of a run, why repeating a run finds the stored result instead of computing it again, which changes make a new run, and how to read a run's record."
camdl-run-scratch: first-fit
---

Every simulation and fit camdl runs is kept in a store, a directory tree under
`results/` in your project. Before camdl runs anything, it works out exactly
what the result will depend on: the compiled model, the backend and time step,
the parameter values, the scenario, the seed. It then looks in the store for a
result computed from those same inputs. If one is there, camdl reads it back
instead of computing it again; if not, it computes the result and stores it
where the next identical request will find it.

This page shows that from the command line: where a run goes, why the second
request is answered from the store, which changes make a new run, and how to
read what the store recorded. It uses the boarding-school SIR model from
[Fitting the boarding-school outbreak](first-fit.qmd), simulated at the
parameter values in `truth.toml` ($R_0 = 3.75$, $\gamma = 0.4$ per day, 763
boys, 3 ill on day 0). Every command on this page ran when the site was built,
and the output under it is what camdl printed. To follow along, copy
[`docs/guide/first-fit/`](https://github.com/vsbuffalo/camdl/tree/main/docs/guide/first-fit)
and run the commands from inside it.

## Where a run is stored

We simulate three stochastic epidemics, one per seed:

```{.camdl-run}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:3
```

camdl ran three cells, one per seed, and stored each as a **leaf** of the store:
a directory holding the trajectory (`traj.tsv`) and a record of the run
(`run.json`), under `results/sims/`. Because the run had several cells, it also
stored the three trajectories side by side as one table, an **ensemble**, under
`results/ensembles/`.

The leaf's directory is named after the run's inputs. Let us look at one:

```{.camdl-run}
ls -d results/sims/*/*/*/*/seed_2-*
```

The path has five levels below `sims/`: the model, the configuration (backend
and time step), the parameter values, the scenario, and the seed. Each level is
written `{label}-{hash}`. The label (`sir_r0`, `chain_binomial-dt0.1`, `base`,
`_none_` for no scenario, `seed_2`) is there for you to read. The eight hex
characters after it are the start of a hash of that level's inputs, and they are
what camdl actually matches on. Two runs whose inputs agree at every level have
the same path and the same **run id**, a 64-character hash computed from all
five levels.

## Running the same thing again

Running the same command again computes nothing:

```{.camdl-run show-match="read from the store|stored"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:3
```

All three cells were read from the store. The same holds for any part of a
request the store already covers. Asking for four seeds reuses the three that
exist and simulates only the fourth:

```{.camdl-run show-match="read from the store|stored"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:4
```

A dry run asks the store the same question without running anything, and lists
every cell as a hit (read back) or a miss (would be simulated):

```{.camdl-run show-match="[hit ]|[miss]|would simulate"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:5 --dry-run
```

::: {.internals title="Why a single-cell run is simulated again"}

A `simulate` with one cell, such as `--seed 7`, does not skip the computation:
it runs the simulation, then finds the stored leaf with the same run id and
keeps it. Before keeping it, camdl compares the trajectory it just computed with
the stored one. They must be byte for byte the same, because a run with a fixed
seed is deterministic. If they ever differ, camdl stops with a `divergent
recompute` error and keeps the new bytes under `results/.quarantine/`: two
different results under one run id mean that something which changes the output
is missing from the inputs camdl hashes, and that is a bug in camdl worth
reporting. A multi-cell run, as above, reads its stored cells back without
recomputing them.

:::

## Changes that keep the same run

Some options change how a run is carried out or where a copy of it is written,
but not what it computes. They do not make a new run. Here we use four threads
and also write the combined trajectory to a file of our own:

```{.camdl-run show-match="read from the store|written"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:3 --parallel 4 -o seeds.tsv
```

The cells were still read from the store; `seeds.tsv` is a copy of the stored
ensemble. The same is true of a `--label`, a display name recorded on the run,
of the progress and verbosity options, and of the name of the model file: a
model renamed or moved, with its contents unchanged, compiles to the same model,
and its earlier runs are still found (camdl prints a warning naming the file
they were first run from, whose name their directories keep).

## Changes that make a new run

Anything that changes the numbers in the trajectory, or which numbers are
stored, is a different run. A new seed draws a new epidemic:

```{.camdl-run show-match="stored"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seed 7
```

Dropping the flow columns from the output changes what the leaf holds, even
though the epidemics are the same ones, so it is a new run too. A dry run shows
that none of the three cells is in the store:

```{.camdl-run show-match="[miss]|would simulate"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:3 --no-flows --dry-run
```

Running it stores three new leaves:

```{.camdl-run show-match="stored"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:3 --no-flows
```

The two column views now sit side by side as two configuration directories
under the one model:

```{.camdl-run}
ls results/sims/sir_r0-*/
```

The same applies to an edit to the model file that changes the compiled model
(a comment does not), to the backend, `--dt`, the horizon, any parameter value
however it is set, the scenario, and the contents of any table or data file a
run reads. camdl's own version is an input as well: the model level includes
the version of the camdl that ran it, so after camdl is upgraded or rebuilt
from another commit, every run is computed again the first time it is asked
for. A result you need to keep across an upgrade should be kept by its files,
which stay readable, not by expecting the store to find it.

## What a run records

`camdl list` shows the runs in the store, newest first, one table per kind of
run:

```{.camdl-run}
camdl list --kind sim
```

`camdl show` prints one run's record, given its directory or the first few
characters of its run id. For the seed-7 run:

```{.camdl-run}
camdl show results/sims/*/*/*/*/seed_7-*
```

`run_id` and `levels` are the run's identity, the hashes the store matches on.
`params`, `seed` and `scenario` are the resolved inputs those hashes were
computed from. `argv`, `created` and `engine` record how and when the run was
made, and by which camdl. The record itself is `run.json` in the leaf's
directory:

```{.camdl-run show-match="run_id|engine_version|label|created_at|camdl_version"}
cat results/sims/*/*/*/*/seed_7-*/run.json
```

`run.json` is what any program reading the store should rely on. The directory
names exist for people to navigate by; a program that wants a run's model,
parameters or seed reads them from the record rather than parsing the path.

## Forcing a run to be computed again

`--force` makes `simulate` compute every cell even when the store holds it:

```{.camdl-run show-match="stored"}
camdl simulate sir-r0.camdl --params truth.toml --seeds 1:3 --force
```

The leaves it replaces are not deleted. They are moved to
`results/.quarantine/`, so a forced run never destroys the result it replaces:

```{.camdl-run}
ls results/.quarantine/
```

`camdl fit run --force` likewise computes a stored fit again and moves the old
one to `results/.quarantine/`.

## Fits

`camdl fit run fit.toml` resolves the fit's identity before it starts, from the
compiled model, the contents of the data files, the fit configuration, the
method and the seed. If the store holds a completed fit with that identity, it
reports a cache hit and returns at once, which is why a fit that took an hour
the first time takes a moment the second. Comments, whitespace and the
`output_dir` and `[provenance]` entries of `fit.toml` are not part of the
identity, so editing them keeps the stored fit. Changing the `[method]` table
or the seed makes a new run alongside the old ones, under the same fit
directory. [The fit workflow](../workflow.md) covers how fits are found by
label and by file.

## Why camdl is built this way

camdl treats a run as a function of its inputs and the store as the table of
that function's values. Keying the table on the inputs themselves, rather than
on a name you choose or a directory you pick, means that the question "have I
already run this?" has an answer camdl can check, and that two people, or one
person on two days, who ask for the same computation get the same stored
result. A result is addressed by what it _is_, so an analysis can cite a run id
and anyone with the store can find exactly that run.

The inputs are hashed after camdl has resolved them, not as you typed them.
Parameter values are hashed as the numbers the simulator uses, after every
`--params` file, scenario and `--param` has been applied; data and table files
are hashed by their contents, so editing a file under the same name makes a new
run; the seed is the one that drives each cell's random numbers, which is why
`--replicates 3` makes three runs from one `--seed`. Two spellings of one
computation are one run, and one spelling of two computations is two.

The two ways the store can be wrong are not equally bad. If camdl hashed
something that does not affect the result, the cost would be a run computed
again that could have been reused. If it failed to hash something that does,
the cost would be a stored result served for a different computation, with
nothing on screen to say so. camdl is built to err toward the first: an input is
hashed unless it is known to affect only how a result is displayed.

The details are in two places.
[Run identity](../internals/engineering/run-identity.qmd), in the internals
section, explains for developers how the hash is computed and what a change to
it touches. The run system specification gives the layout of
[the content-addressed store](../camdl-run-spec.md#21-the-content-addressed-store)
and the steps
[from a job to a path](../camdl-run-spec.md#37-from-a-job-to-a-path-run-identity).
